text:
jules: Quick note — the new Next quickstart (kitchen-sink) is shipping with telemetry enabled by default and Node SDK retry behavior is not matching Python. Hit this while onboarding a customer: SSR pages intermittently 401 during auth rotation and client-side streams drop without retries.

lia: Ugh, thanks for flagging. Can you paste the repro steps and logs?

jules: Steps: 1) npx create-next-app --example redwood/next-kitchen 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY env and run `npm run dev` 3) open /chat SSR route that uses server-side Redwood client. After a few requests auth rotates and subsequent SSR render fails with 401, then stream endpoints fail with ECONNRESET.

jules: Logs: ```
ERR 401 Unauthorized - /api/ssr-chat  
  at authClient.rotateToken (/app/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/auth.js:78:23)
  at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)
ERR ECONNRESET - stream closed during chunked response
```

mike: That stack looks like token rotation happens async but SSR path doesn't await new token. Could be middleware mismatch between edge/runtime and node adapter.

sam: Also noticed Node SDK has only one immediate retry with no exponential backoff. Python has jittered backoff and header-based retry hints. Not parity.

kevin: The telemetry bit — which flag? I thought we default off for sample apps.

jules: In the starter repo package.json we set `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1` in .env.example and README says opt-out via env. Surprised to see opt-in-by-default in starter. Customers likely confused.

lia: Agree we should not enable telemetry by default in tutorial repos. Low friction for DX but bad privacy opt defaults.

mike: For retry parity, quick patch: add exponential backoff wrapper in Node client around request loop, honor `retry-after` header, and propagate retry hints to streaming layer. I can prototype.

sam: Would be great to get small unit tests too — simulate 401 followed by 200 after rotation so SSR path waits for token.

jules: Minimal repro snippet I used server-side: ```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
export async function getServerSideProps(ctx) {
  const res = await client.chat.create({ messages: [{role:'user', content:'hi'}] });
  return { props: { reply: res.text } }
}
```

jules: When token rotation races, client.chat.create throws before rotation completes. Might need internal lock or refresh-in-flight promise.

kevin: OK - here's proposed plan: (1) revert telemetry default in starter -> change .env.example and README (2) add small retry/backoff shim to Node SDK + tests (3) fix SSR token rotation by gating in-flight refresh or exposing `await client.ensureReady()` for SSR flows.

lia: +1. Also add a line in quickstart README explaining how to disable telemetry and how to configure retry policy.

devex-bot: Assigned issue #DEVEX-487 to mike for Node SDK retry/backoff prototype.

mike: I'll open a draft PR with tests by EOD tomorrow. Will include changelog and mention telemetry revert.

sam: Ping me on the PR for review — I'll add the SSR gating test.

jules: Thanks team. One more UX nit: sample app's onboarding prompt references the old `OPENAI_API_KEY` env which confused users. I'll send a tiny PR to update env var naming while I'm at it. :sweat_smile:

kevin: Nice catch. Please include that in the quickstart revert PR if small.

lia: Great thread. After fixes we should run the quickstart through a fresh user test to confirm onboarding friction is gone. :eyes:

jules: Will do.

mike: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-kitchen/pull/122 (WIP) — includes telemetry revert and retry shim prototype.

sam: Reviewed initial code. Suggest using a jittered backoff util from /lib/backoff so we don't duplicate.

jules: Awesome, closing the loop here. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
